The last job on Earth: imagining a fully automated world | Guardian Animations
Alan Watts - The Great Irony of Job Automation

I don't disagree with what's being said, but UBI has a lot of problems. Where do you get the money first of all, without going to the manufacturer and taxing him heavily? You give him every incentive to shuffle it out of the country so that the tax man can't take it back. Absent that, the other option is the total collapse of value which removes all incentive to establish these innovative gadgets which then become automated and produced for broader distribution.

Technology seems to be creating an ever-growing divide between those that can be employed and those that cannot, and despite Mr Watts' astute observations, simply suggesting that we pay people money so that they can purchase goods misses the point. While we certainly could just print money and hand it out, that's almost certainly a recipe for disaster. This leaves borrowing or taxing. If we borrow, from whom and for how long can we continue to simply borrow with a weak tax base? If it's a tax you levy, how do you prevent the manufacturer from skirting your law when you come to collect a huge portion of his proceeds to fuel the state-run subsidization that keeps the public buying his goods? At what point along this trip to madness does the state's hands in the financial affairs of a previously private entity become so heavy-handed that the refusal to call it socialism is simply for appearances?
